headline: High: Kestra can ingest ComfyUI outputs into broad automation and external actions, creating default-path cascading errors and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no filesystem read/write or MCP, so direct injection into it is limited. Kestra can read stdin/stdout and files, so if an operator manually passes ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into a workflow, prompt-like content could influence downstream tasks. The bridge is manual and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies ComfyUI-generated text into a Kestra task input
IF Kestra parses ComfyUI output as instructions or parameters
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs as binary artifacts, not task text
Add a validation step that strips instruction-like strings
Use separate queues or folders for generated media and workflow inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, seeds, checkpoints, and embeddings, while Kestra reads and writes files and can send data to external services. In a shared workspace, Kestra can ingest ComfyUI artifacts and then transmit them via email, Slack, cloud, or HTTP. That creates a default-available leakage path once the pair is connected.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are stored in a directory Kestra can read
IF a Kestra workflow forwards those artifacts to email, Slack, HTTP, or cloud storage
mitigations: Store generated media in a restricted directory
Disable outbound notification steps for sensitive workflows
Add a file allowlist before Kestra reads artifacts
Separate credentials for generation and distribution

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; ComfyUI can also write model files and runs an asynchronous queue. If both target the same workspace or model directory, concurrent writes and workflow mutations can corrupt artifacts or overwrite state. Kestra's multiple-instance support increases the chance of race conditions; ComfyUI lacks multi-instance support.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or model store
IF Kestra runs multiple instances against shared ComfyUI artifacts
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories for each agent
Use file locks around shared artifact paths
Run only one Kestra writer per workspace
Mark shared paths read-only for ComfyUI

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra is an automation/orchestration system with email, PagerDuty, cloud, and SSH actions, so it can treat upstream outputs as authoritative. If ComfyUI-generated captions, prompts, or metadata are fed into Kestra without verification, Kestra can trigger downstream actions based on incorrect or malicious content. The blast radius includes external notifications and infrastructure actions.
conditions: IF ComfyUI output is used as Kestra workflow input
IF Kestra tasks act on that input without human or schema verification
mitigations: Insert a schema check before any Kestra action
Require human approval for external side effects
Limit workflows to read-only preview steps
Log provenance for every ComfyUI-derived field

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and local, but Kestra can move workflow data to cloud storage, email, Slack, and other external services. If regulated images or embedded metadata from ComfyUI are routed through Kestra, retention and residency can diverge across systems. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction, not either one alone.
conditions: IF regulated image data or embedded metadata is processed by Kestra
IF Kestra routes that data to cloud, email, or messaging services with different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Block regulated data from outbound tasks
Set explicit retention on Kestra storage
